Title: Qud Expanded Community Edition
Description:
[h1]Qud Expanded Community Edition[/h1]
[i]A community-maintained fork of [b]Caves of Qud Expanded[/b] by Mura.[/i]

This is a [b]separate mod[/b]. It does not replace, modify, or take over the original, which remains Mura's and is still available here:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1134036260]Caves of Qud Expanded[/url]

[h1]What you get[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Psionic Adept[/b] — a third genotype for players who would rather find their build than plan it. No mutations, the fewest stat points in the game, the most skill points per level, and power that comes from psionic chips: they cannot be bought or built and only come out of chests. A True Kin saves for the implant it wants; an Adept wears what it finds. 18 subtypes, sprites by Noble Lark.
[*][b]144 psionic chips[/b] — implantable chips granting real mutations to genotypes that cannot mutate. Every one can be found.
[*][b]Complete weapon and armor families[/b] — bronze through zetachrome, one- and two-handed, consistent in stats and price at every tier.
[*][b]New weapon classes[/b] — katanas, rapiers, halberds, greataxes, greatswords, warhammers, greathammers, wristblades, glaives, spears and quarterstaves.
[*][b]Effect ammunition[/b] — six arrows, four shotgun shells, and the scour slug, which rusts what your target carries instead of hurting them.
[*][b]Anthro mutations[/b] — Tail, Keen Smell and Fangs, for the animal in the build rather than on the sprite.
[*][b]Sleep, and what it costs you[/b] — go long enough without it and you fall down where you stand. Where you sleep is the decision: a settlement is safe, bare ground is not. Sleep right through and you dream, sometimes of somewhere you have never been. [b]Off by default.[/b]
[*][b]Injury and illness you can act on[/b] — wounds that rest will not close, diseases that say what is happening while you can still act, and weapons that wear out the way armor already does.
[*][b]Thirteen books and four bookshelves[/b] about the places they stand in — Grit Gate, Hydropon, Yd Freehold and Redrock.
[*][b]Eighteen more trinkets[/b], each doing one small useless thing, half of them proof against a screwdriver.
[*][b]More to forage and cook[/b] — bruisemoss, rimeburr, shadetooth and broadglove, and village dishes made from the local preserved plant.
[*][b]44 creature colour variants[/b] — brindle dogs, black goats, cinder glowcrows. Cosmetic, and the ordinary animal stays the common one.
[*][b]Names, genders and pronouns[/b] — wider name pools, optional gendered endings, thirteen genders and fourteen pronoun sets, all of which Qud already had. Items can be named for a pride flag.
[*][b]A home base in Joppa[/b] — bed, storage, oven, becoming nook.
[*][b]Dozens of smaller repairs[/b] — gates that swing shut behind you, liquids gathered into one container, creatures you can ask the name of, arrows you can pick back up.
[*][b]Skill and economy retuning[/b] — more mutation and skill points, eased requirements, adjusted costs. All optional.
[/list]

[h1]Options[/h1]
[b]Thirty-four settings in Qud's own options menu, under Mods.[/b] Each defaults to what the mod has always done, except where marked. Play it as tuned, or dial any of it back to vanilla.
[list]
[*]Mutation points — 16 by default, anything from 0 to 24
[*]Mutant hit points per level, and extra skill points per level
[*]Extra starting skills, eased requirements, retuned skill point costs
[*]Starting reputation bonus with Joppa, and the Joppa home base — [b]bonus off by default[/b]
[*]Psionic chips in loot — off closes the supply completely
[*]Chip Interface slots — a True Kin's two, and the ones on other humanoids
[*]Graded burden — [b]off by default[/b]
[*]How your own random name sounds, your gender, and your pronouns
[*]Anthro mutations - this fork's animal-trait mutations
[*]Sleep, and the four systems that ride on it — [b]off by default[/b]
[*]The Six Day Stilt as a market, and the two notoriety systems — [b]off by default[/b]
[/list]

Psionic Adepts are unaffected throughout: their numbers are the genotype, not an addition to a vanilla one.

[h1]New in 2.15.0[/h1]
Five changes to things already here. [b]Nothing new to switch on.[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Heightened smell costs 5 points, up from 3.[/b] It finds hostiles through walls and names them. At rank 1 it reaches 9 squares against hearing's 5, so it identifies what hearing cannot even detect. Priced as the ambush immunity it is.
[*][b]Fangs answer to your training.[/b] The bite ran at a flat 20% and discarded everything the Multiweapon line gives it, so training the obvious skills made it relatively worse. Now 20% untrained to 40% trained - and Single Weapon Fighting silences it properly at last.
[*][b]A dream is for a night, not a nap.[/b] Dreams followed every sleep, so lying down at one point of fatigue was a dream every 24 turns. They now ask that you were tired first, and come half the time.
[*][b]Tiredness arrives more slowly.[/b] A full meter takes about 3.8 days unhurried rather than 3. Fighting for it still halves that.
[*][b]Being weary costs something.[/b] It was a word in the status bar. Now something you counted on occasionally gutters out - and exhaustion reaches everyone, not only mental mutants.
[/list]

Two of these take something away mid-save: the bite under Single Weapon Fighting, and dreams from naps.
[h1]Compatibility[/h1]
[b]Do not enable this and the original Caves of Qud Expanded at the same time.[/b] Pick one — a continuation defines the same 36 script types, so Qud reports a conflict and whichever loads first wins. Saves do not carry across either.

[b]You no longer need The Grand Bazaar or Experience Curve Beta.[/b] Both are part of this mod now, behind their own options.
[list]
[*][b]The Grand Bazaar[/b] — to keep running the original, turn [i]the Six Day Stilt[/i] option off, or you get two of each merchant.
[*][b]Experience Curve Beta[/b] — safe to leave enabled alongside, and nothing to set: this mod's own [i]experience curve[/i] option is the one that takes effect.
[/list]

Every change this fork makes to a vanilla record is a merge, never a replacement, so it should not discard what future Qud patches add, and plays nicely with most other mods. Please report compatibility issues via Steam or GitHub.

[h1]Version and saves[/h1]
[b]2.15.0.[/b] Loads on 2.14.x saves - no new character needed. Every change reaches a character you are already playing, except heightened smell's cost, which is read at character creation.

Coming from Mura's original, [b]start a new character[/b]: identifiers changed during the fork, and Qud writes those into save files.
